confirmedFindings: The third Python block fails with NameError for private_key when run alone, in both Japanese and English. All three blocks run in order successfully, so do not describe the sequential example as broken. The current signature example also reuses the encryption example key.

The RSA formula covers every 0 <= M < N, but its Euler-theorem proof step needs coprimality. With p=61, q=53 and M=61, M^phi mod N is 1220 rather than 1, while RSA roundtrip returns 61. All 3,233 message representatives roundtrip with the toy key. This is not a general security proof.

The existing RSA-2048/SHA-256 OAEP example has a 190-byte maximum message. 190 bytes roundtrip and 191 are rejected. Wrong label and altered ciphertext fail; the article does not explain this payload bound.

Signing is described and drawn as private-key encryption/public-key decryption, while its actual code uses RSASSA-PSS. The official implementation documentation distinguishes PSS signing from OAEP encryption and their encodings.
The cited FIPS 186-4 is withdrawn as of 2024-02-03 and superseded by FIPS 186-5. The current FIPS 186-5 landing page has a 2025 errata planning note; that errata file has not been reviewed.

Certificate-chain validation is more than directly verifying a server certificate with the root key. RFC 5280 defines a path from a trust anchor; TLS 1.3 separately negotiates key exchange, authentication and record protection and supports PSK modes.
